item.text:
**Verdict**
2024 looks **mixed but mildly positive overall** for 8B.7. The clearest movement in the intended direction is macroeconomic: inflation fell materially by year-end and growth/fiscal handling held up despite shocks. The main drag is that the flagship rice-affordability outcome lagged or underperformed, and civic-space outcomes did not clearly improve.

**Accepted Claims**

- **[IMF concludes 2024 Article IV consultation](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/12/17/pr-24478-philippines-imf-concludes-2024-article-iv-consultation)** | International Monetary Fund | December 19, 2024 | The IMF said the Philippines handled external headwinds well, growth stayed resilient, inflation averaged 3.2% in 2024, and fiscal consolidation was underway. This is the strongest independent broad signal that the year moved in the direction of the administration’s stability and growth goals. | QIDs: 8B.7

- **[2024 annual inflation report](https://psa.gov.ph/price-indices/cpi-ir/node/1684065571)** | Philippine Statistics Authority | 2024 annual report | PSA reported annual inflation at 3.2% in 2024 versus 6.0% in 2023, with food inflation easing from 8.0% to 4.5%. That is a real directional improvement on the cost-of-living problem Marcos kept emphasizing, though it does not by itself prove policy causation. | QIDs: 8B.7

- **[Philippines posts monthly budget surplus](https://interaksyon.philstar.com/business/2024/11/27/287793/philippines-budget-surplus-at-6-3-billion-in-october/)** | Reuters / Interaksyon | November 27, 2024 | Reuters reported an October budget surplus and a smaller year-to-date deficit than a year earlier. This supports a modest claim of improved fiscal handling, while still leaving overall fiscal stress in place. | QIDs: 8B.7

- **[Unemployment rate in April 2024](https://psa.gov.ph/content/unemployment-rate-april-2024-was-estimated-40-percent?vcode=2LnTw)** | Philippine Statistics Authority | June 6, 2024 | Unemployment fell to 4.0%, though underemployment remained high. This is a limited positive outcome for the growth-and-jobs agenda, but it is not a broad labor-market breakthrough. | QIDs: 8B.7

- **[NEDA: reduced rice tariffs failed to lower prices](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/)** | GMA News Online | December 10, 2024 | The main rice-affordability intervention had only partial or weak retail pass-through. That is the clearest negative outcome against Marcos’s food-price claims, even after allowing for lags and typhoons. | QIDs: 8B.7

- **[Philippine inflation quickens again in March as rice soars](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippine-inflation-quickens-again-in-march-as-rice-soars-3366872)** | Reuters | April 4, 2024 | Early-2024 rice inflation hit a 15-year high and monetary conditions stayed tight. This is important counterevidence because the year began under severe external and inherited pressure, so the later improvement was not immediate. | QIDs: 8B.7

- **[Digital News Report 2024: Philippines](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines)** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | Red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos. That means outcomes in civic openness did not clearly move in the direction implied by his pro-press rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

- **[2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html)** | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | The report said credible killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, media restrictions, and threats to labor activists remained. That is strong negative evidence that the broader rights environment did not improve cleanly in 2024. | QIDs: 8B.7, 8B.6

**Bottom Line**
- **Positive:** inflation, food inflation, and fiscal management improved by year-end, and labor-market conditions did not collapse.
- **Negative:** rice affordability did not clearly improve quickly, and civic-space outcomes remained poor.
- **Overall:** Marcos’s 2024 outcomes moved **somewhat** toward the stated goals, but only **selectively** and with major gaps.

**Search Gap**
- I found strong independent macro series, but fewer independent year-end outcome datasets for service delivery and civic-space claims.
- The best evidence on those areas is a mix of surveys, human-rights reporting, and official releases, so the confidence on non-macro outcomes should stay lower than the confidence on inflation and growth.
